❓ Common Questions

Questions Parents Often Ask

We've got answers to help ease your mind before your child's visit.

When should my child have their first dental visit?

+

The American Academy of Pediatric Dentistry recommends your child's first dental visit by age 1 or within 6 months of their first tooth appearing. Early visits help us detect any concerns and educate parents on proper care techniques.

How can I help my child not be afraid of the dentist?

+

Talk positively about dental visits, read dental-themed books, and play "pretend dentist" at home. Our team also uses gentle desensitization techniques — we show kids every tool before we use it and narrate everything we're doing.

Do you accept dental insurance?

+

Yes! We accept most major dental insurance plans including Delta Dental, Cigna, Aetna, and many more. We also work with Medicaid/Medi-Cal and offer flexible payment plans. Contact our office for specific coverage questions.

Are dental X-rays safe for children?

+

Absolutely. We use digital X-rays which emit up to 90% less radiation than traditional film X-rays. We also use protective lead aprons, and we only take X-rays when clinically necessary based on your child's individual risk factors.

What should I do if my child has a dental emergency?

+

Call us immediately at (949) 555-1234. We reserve same-day appointments for dental emergencies. If a tooth is knocked out, keep it moist (in milk or water), and bring it with you. For after-hours emergencies, our voicemail provides guidance.

How often should my child visit the dentist?

+

Most children benefit from dental checkups every 6 months. However, some children with higher cavity risk may need more frequent visits. We'll recommend a schedule tailored specifically to your child's needs at their first appointment.

🌈 Kids Corner

Fun Dental Facts for Kids!

🦷

Your teeth are the only part of your body that can't heal themselves — that's why brushing and flossing is so important!

👅

Your tongue is covered in about 10,000 tiny taste buds — and it's also home to more bacteria than a tooth!

😁

Tooth enamel is the hardest substance your body makes — even harder than bone!

🐘

Elephants grow 6 sets of teeth in their lifetime. Humans only get 2 sets — so take good care of them!

🪥 Perfect Brushing in 4 Steps!

1

Apply pea-sized fluoride toothpaste on a soft-bristled brush made for kids.

2

Brush at a 45° angle against the gumline for 2 full minutes — use a timer or brushing song!

3

Brush all surfaces — outside, inside, and the chewing tops. Don't forget your tongue!

4

Spit and rinse — and you're done! Remember to floss once a day too!

New Patients

Welcome to the Sproutly Family!

We're so excited to meet your little one! Here's everything you need to know to make your first visit smooth, comfortable, and fun.

What to Expect

Your Child's First Visit, Step by Step

We've designed our new patient experience to be as relaxed and welcoming as possible for the whole family.

1

Warm Welcome & Tour

You'll be greeted by our friendly front desk team. We'll give your child a quick tour of the office — our "treasure chest," the cool dental chair, and all the fun equipment. No surprises!

2

Medical & Dental History Review

We'll review the health forms you completed online, discuss any concerns or medical conditions, and chat about your child's current dental habits and history.

3

Gentle Exam & X-Rays (If Appropriate)

Our dentist will conduct a thorough but gentle oral examination. For most children over 3, we'll take a few digital X-rays to get a complete picture of dental development.

4

Professional Cleaning & Fluoride

Our hygienist will perform a gentle cleaning, demonstrate proper brushing and flossing techniques, and apply a fluoride treatment to strengthen enamel.

5

Discussion & Care Plan

We'll meet with you privately to review findings, answer every question you have, and create a personalized care plan. You'll leave with a clear picture of your child's dental health.

6

Prize & Next Appointment

Every child gets to pick a prize from our treasure chest — a Sproutly tradition! We'll schedule your next checkup before you leave so you're all set.

💡 Parent Tips

How to Prepare Your Child for Their Visit

A little preparation at home can make all the difference in how your child feels at the dentist.

📖

Read Dental Books Together

Dental-themed children's books ("The Berenstain Bears Visit the Dentist" is a classic!) help normalize the experience before it happens.

🎭

Play Pretend Dentist

Take turns being the "dentist" with a toothbrush and mirror. This familiarity with the examination reduces anxiety on the real day.

💬

Use Positive Language

Avoid words like "hurt," "needle," or "shot." Instead, use our friendly words — "tickle brush," "counting teeth," "sleepy juice."

🌅

Schedule at the Right Time

Book morning appointments when children are well-rested. Avoid scheduling during nap times or when they're typically hungry.

😊

Stay Calm Yourself

Children pick up on parental anxiety. Speak about the visit with excitement and matter-of-factness — "We're going to see the tooth helpers!"

🏆

Plan a Reward After

Promise a fun activity after the visit (playground, favorite meal). Having something to look forward to creates a positive association.
